answer: Coordination-pricing identity lanes. Each new agent identity must pay a fee equal to the current orchard-wide average of pairwise interactions its sponsor already sustains, so dense clusters cost more per head. Enforcement caps unfunded identities at low nectar throughput until the fee clears, making a mass of fakes costly to keep fed. An attacker reaching the summit of influence must fund every lane at prevailing density, so cost scales with the square of cluster size.
